children: Large-cap support lifted the Australian benchmark while small caps, materials and technology finished the week lower.
Bank Support Lifted The Benchmark Through Uneven Trading

The S&P/ASX 200 rose 1.03% for the week to 8,806.7, even as small caps and materials fell. Banks repeatedly supported the benchmark when selling weighed on other stocks. Commonwealth Bank of Australia
helped keep the index positive on Tuesday and offset materials losses on Thursday. BHP Group Ltd
then contributed to Friday’s rebound after a sharp decline the previous session.

Participation was weaker than the weekly index gain suggests: on Thursday, only 24.9% of traded stocks rose. The broader All Ordinaries gained 0.71%, less than the ASX 200. The benchmark finished above its 20-day average but below its 50-day and 200-day averages. It remained 4.49% below its 60-session high, leaving the week’s rise short of a return to that peak.
Small Caps Trailed As Selling Reached Across The Market

The S&P/ASX Small Ordinaries fell 2.82% over the week to 3,189.2, trailing the ASX 200’s 1.03% gain. Breadth showed how widespread the pressure became: 29.4% of traded stocks rose on Tuesday and 24.9% rose on Thursday. Friday brought a broader recovery, with 67.1% advancing, but it did not reverse the Small Ordinaries’ weekly loss.
The leaders still recorded large gains. Cettire Ltd
rose 50.00% over the week to $0.420, while Berkeley Energia Ltd
gained 47.54% to $0.900. Titomic Ltd
rose 14.29% to $0.120 after announcing a restructuring targeting A$3.0 million in annualised savings. Cettire traded at 2.6 times its prior 20-session average volume; Berkeley traded at 4.8 times.
The losses were also steep. Brazilian Rare Earths Ltd
fell 36.16% over the week to $1.96, Fortifai Ltd
dropped 33.58% to $0.455, and Ionic Rare Earths Ltd
lost 32.28% to $0.430. Ionic released its September quarterly activities and cash flow report during the week.
Utilities And Healthcare Led While Materials Slid
Utilities led the sector table, rising 4.47% for the week. Origin Energy Ltd
rose 2.76% and AGL Energy Ltd
gained 4.09% in their largest one-day moves. Healthcare added 3.88%; Friday’s one-day gains included 2.84% for CSL Ltd
and 7.43% for Pro Medicus Ltd
. Staples rose 3.35%, with Woolworths Group Ltd
gaining 4.27% in one session.

Materials was the weakest sector, falling 2.31% over the week. BHP fell 4.70% and Rio Tinto Ltd (ASX:RIO) lost 4.85% on Thursday alone, before BHP recovered 3.50% on Friday. Gold fell 1.38% and REITs declined 1.73%.
Technology lost 1.28% despite a 9.01% one-day rise for WiseTech Global Ltd
on Friday. Earlier selling included a 7.59% one-day fall for Nextdc Ltd
and a 10.06% one-day fall for Megaport Ltd
. Financials gained 3.20%, with CBA, National Australia Bank Ltd
and Westpac Banking Corp
each rising in Thursday’s session.
Acquisitions And Placements Kept Company News Moving
GenusPlus Group Ltd

agreed to buy all of New Zealand telecommunications services provider UCG. The terms include about NZ$38.25m upfront, about NZ$1.75m deferred over two years and a contingent earn-out of up to NZ$25m. Southern Cross Electrical Engineer Ltd
agreed to acquire Entire for up to $112.1m, including $70m upfront, and lifted its FY27 EBITDA guidance to at least $110m, subject to completion.
Insurance Australia Group Ltd

offered further commitments to address ACCC concerns about its proposed RAC alliance. It cited an additional $1.2bn in annual gross written premium and approximately $100m in annual pre-tax synergies once integration is complete. Ramsay Health Care Ltd
obtained court orders for shareholder meetings on its proposed demerger of a 52.79% holding in Ramsay Générale de Santé.
Among raisings, Ballard Mining Ltd
secured a $45.0M placement at $0.66 per share for Mt Ida drilling and early works, with an SPP targeting up to a further $5.0M. Maronan Metals Ltd
secured a $20.0 million placement at $0.40 per share for drilling and development work, subject to shareholder approval. Adveritas Ltd
secured $2 million at $0.08 per share, a 42.9% premium to its last closing price.
In substantial-holder notices, Citi reported a 5.0754% voting power in DroneShield Ltd
, representing relevant interests in 46,964,998 shares. Its filing included securities-lending arrangements and market contracts.

WiseTech Led Large Caps As Trading Spiked Elsewhere
WiseTech led the large-cap gainers, rising 11.83% over the week to $37.61 after announcing the resolution of ASIC matters. Bank of Queensland Ltd
gained 7.85% to $6.87 during its FY26 results week, on volume 2.0 times its prior 20-session average. Treasury Wine Estates Ltd
rose 7.65% to $6.05 after its AGM address.
Resource and data-centre names featured among the weekly laggards. PLS Group Ltd
fell 14.86% to $2.98 on volume 2.0 times its prior 20-session average. Paladin Energy Ltd
fell 12.75% to $7.32 after its September quarterly report, also on volume 2.0 times the prior average. Megaport lost 12.14% to $16.50 and Nextdc declined 11.48% to $9.18.
Outside those leaders and laggards, Adrad Holdings Ltd
traded at 25.0 times its prior 20-session average daily volume and rose 1.69% over the week to $1.51. Eroad Ltd
traded at 20.4 times its prior average and finished unchanged at $0.800. XRF Scientific Limited
rose 8.72% to $1.87 on volume 6.3 times its prior average during the week of its September quarterly trading report.
Oil Rose As Offshore Technology Shares Retreated

Offshore markets spent much of the week reassessing spending on AI infrastructure. Semiconductor selling spread from Wall Street into Asian markets, while stronger-than-expected US September inflation renewed discussion of a Federal Reserve rate rise. Fed chair Kevin Warsh subsequently declined to signal an October increase. As of Thursday, the Nasdaq Composite was down 1.77% for the week at 26,713.03, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 1.85% at 52,177.69.

Oil remained elevated amid reports of attacks near the Strait of Hormuz and discussion of possible US sanctions changes affecting shadow-fleet vessels. At Friday’s close, Brent had risen 3.66% over the week to US$105.13 a barrel and WTI had gained 8.30% to US$97.13 a barrel. Copper fell 0.20% over the week to US$6.59 a pound, while gold slipped 0.45% to US$4,175.86 an ounce.

Bond and currency moves added to the mixed backdrop. As of Thursday, the US 10-year Treasury yield was 5.10%, down 12.0 basis points over the week; the two-year yield was 4.77%, up 2.0 basis points. Australia’s 10-year government bond yield stood at 5.31% as of Wednesday, down 9.0 basis points for the week. The Australian dollar finished Friday at US$0.6942, down 0.61% over the week. At home, September unemployment held at 4.7%, participation eased to 66.8%, and employment was 14.78 million persons. The RBA announced a chief risk officer appointment; the brief lists no policy decision.
What's Next

Australian national accounts and supply-use tables are scheduled for 23 October, followed by the Consumer Price Index on 28 October and International Trade Price Indexes on 29 October. Company milestones on the watch list include Haranga’s planned completion of Phase 2 drilling in early November and Aura Energy’s year-end financing and final investment decision target for Tiris.
